facts.text: Played as a freshman guard for the SUNY Potsdam women's basketball team, 2015-16
Passed U.S. Figure Skating's Senior Moves in the Field gold test as a Potsdam Figure Skating Club skater, 2022
Recognized for New Product Idea at Clarkson University's Ignite Expo as a Clarkson School student
Scored a goal in Clarkson's 4-3 ECAC-opening win at Harvard, Oct 30, 2026
Recorded a power-play assist in Clarkson's 4-1 win at Dartmouth, Oct 31, 2026
Assisted on two Clarkson goals, including the eventual game-winner, in the 4-3 win at Harvard, Oct 30, 2026

Co-authored a 2022 British Journal of Occupational Therapy study that found no minimal clinically important difference for the Beery-Buktenica Developmental Test of Visual-Motor Integration in children with autism spectrum disorder
Became a manuscript reviewer for the Journal of Clinical Education in Physical Therapy, 2025
Became a manuscript reviewer for the Journal of Allied Health, 2026
Joined the board of the Saranac Lake Young Arts Association as treasurer, 2024
Co-authored a cross-cultural study of dietary supplement attitudes and practices, presented at the American Society for Nutrition's Nutrition 2025 conference, May 2025
Entered the New York City market as Anew Café & Goods became the first New York City café to carry Vivid Coffee's beans, Oct 2026
From the Heart Cabinetry was awarded $95,000 in Northern New York Power Proceeds fund benefits toward purchasing its Potsdam facility, Nov 2018

note: PM run (second of the day, twice-daily cadence). Checked 75, filed 13 facts across 9 people, each parent-verified on its source page and read back in the Sheet exactly once. Fresh sweep found two winners, both from Clarkson's ECAC-opening weekend: Janelle Evans scored in the 4-3 win at Harvard (Harvard University Athletics, published Oct 30, 2026) and added a power-play assist at Dartmouth the next day (Clarkson University Athletics, published Oct 31, 2026); Isa Goettl assisted on two goals at Harvard, including the eventual game-winner (published Oct 30, 2026). Rotation filings: Breanne Sapp played as a freshman guard for SUNY Potsdam's women's basketball team in 2015-16 (her record already covered her Potsdam Central career and her later police and sheriff work); Dillynn Grant passed U.S. Figure Skating's Senior Moves in the Field gold test as a Potsdam Figure Skating Club skater in 2022; William Dunphey was recognized for New Product Idea at Clarkson University's Ignite Expo, a separate recognition from his team project's Third Place prize already on file. Compounding lane (first run): 5 people compounded (Richard Haller, Alisha Ohl, Samantha Marocco, Ian Bailey, Eric Criscitello); 7 facts filed across 4 of them — Alisha Ohl's 2022 British Journal of Occupational Therapy study; four Samantha Marocco items from her Clarkson page (reviewer for the Journal of Clinical Education in Physical Therapy from 2025 and the Journal of Allied Health from 2026, Saranac Lake Young Arts Association board treasurer from 2024, and a Nutrition 2025 conference paper); Ian Bailey's Vivid Coffee entering New York City through Anew Café & Goods in Oct 2026; and the $95,000 New York Power Authority award toward From the Heart Cabinetry's facility purchase in Nov 2018. The lane also flagged one correction for JD: Ian Bailey's record says he founded Vivid Coffee in Burlington, but Seven Days shows he started it in Winooski in 2015 and opened in Burlington in Nov 2020 — it sits in Research Command as a conflict card, not overwritten. Lane metrics: 8 candidates, 1 correction, 5 loop closures, 26 discards. Most of this rotation's batch claims (among them Michael Jent, Eli Larson, Julia Fulton, Danielle Caskinett, Destiny Snyder, Olivia Goodrow, Eric Criscitello's takeover facts, Jake Seguin, Cecilie Smith, and Hannah Braun) were already on file in the live Sheet even though the baked profiles looked empty, and were discarded rather than re-filed.
